the_cavern.text: For generations your people have dug toward God at the bottom of the world. The bright stones in the deep shafts are said to be divine light leaking through the earth. You keep the miners' lamps. Now a crew has broken into a cavern with a black lake and pale creatures nesting along its shore.

choices.text: Go down with the surveyors and inspect the cavern
Ask the high priest what the discovery means

the_shore.text: The creatures withdraw from your lamp. Their eggs lie under ledges near fractures in the rock. The surveyors fear that drilling beneath the lake could flood the lower tunnels and destroy the only place the creatures can breed.

choices.text: Map the cracks and bring the measurements to the settlement
Mark the nesting ledges and ask the miners to avoid them

text.value: The high priest says the creatures were placed there to guide the miners. The surveyors say a new shaft could drown the people below. Both accounts ask you to trust a path you cannot see.
The high priest calls the cavern a sign and orders a new shaft beneath the lake. Your mother says the same words were used before your father died in an unsafe collapse.

choices.text: Lay the measurements on the chapel altar and challenge the order
Keep tending the lamps and let the elders decide

the_congregation.text: The settlement argues for three days. Miners describe the fractures; priests describe what the bright stones have meant to families for generations. No one can prove what waits at the bottom of the world.

choices.text: Vote to seal the lowest shaft until a safe route is found
Support the new shaft; the search is the community's oldest promise

the_lake.text: The decision is made at the cavern's edge. The priests say the faith is being tested; the miners say lives are being weighed. Beneath the lamps, the pale creatures move quietly through their dark water.

choices.text: Shade your lamp and watch the creatures emerge
Raise the lamps and lead the next crew toward the deep

patient_light.text: The shaft is sealed while the surveyors search for another route. The priest calls it a failure of faith; your mother calls it a decision made with open eyes. The lake remains, and so do the people who depend on the tunnels above it.

deeper.text: The new shaft descends slowly, with extra supports and a crew that knows the risks. You do not find God that season. You do find another vein of shining stone, which the children call a promise and the miners call a warning.
